Monthly Surface Water Extent

Seasonal Context
Wet Event Characterisation

A wet event begins once extent climbs above 0.3% (baseline 0.2% plus a margin sized to this record's own month-to-month noise) and continues until it falls back below 0.2% -- hysteresis, so a wobbling recession is not counted as several separate floods. Events shorter than 1 month(s) are dropped; episodes closer than 1 month(s) apart are merged into one.

Low-Extent Spells

A low-extent spell is a run of at least 2 consecutive months below 0.1% (baseline 0.2% minus a margin sized to the same noise scale), counted independently of wet events -- a catchment that never floods can still have long low-extent spells. About 30.6% of this record's months sit below that line, so a spell describes a sustained below-typical period, not an absence of water.
